items.title: Ralph LaLama interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 23, 2010
items.q: So I used to sub on the band. My first gig in New York was with Mel and Thad, but it wasn’t the big band, it was a quintet.

ctx.x: So he wouldn’t ask you do to anything that he wouldn’t do.

That’s right. That’s what I got from him. You know what I mean? So to me that’s what I mean, I mean he’s crazy but I could dig it. I mean technically, on that band you played much more notes. I don’t mean complicated but for me as a saxophone player I learned a lot about the saxophone technique because of some of the music he played. It was like hard, another step. Okay? And then with Mel and Thad, when I got to New York, I mean I knew Thad. I met Thad at Youngstown. Tony Leonardi got Thad to come to Youngstown.…
You said something yesterday, you said you learned more on that gig on the first few weeks than you did in college. What do you learn on that first — I mean what was so memorable?
